artworks.title: The Pleiades
artworks.description: Vedder's Metropolitan Museum canvas dances the seven daughters of Atlas and the Oceanid Pleione — Maia, Electra, Taygete, Alcyone, Celaeno, Sterope, and Merope. The mother herself stays off-stage; her name is the constellation's root and the painting's genealogical key.

popCulture.title: Pleiades (star cluster)
popCulture.description: Messier 45 still carries Pleione's name in the cluster and in the star Pleione (28 Tauri) — the Oceanid mother fixed among her daughters in the winter sky.

popCulture.title: Pleione (mythology)
popCulture.description: Oceanid wife of Atlas, mother of the Pleiades (and in some accounts the Hyades) — protectress of flocks and sailing whose name means increase.

popCulture.title: Pleiades (Greek mythology)
popCulture.description: The seven sisters born to Pleione and Atlas on Cyllene — the genealogical fact every ancient astronomer and poet repeats when the cluster rises.
